pending_interview.category: Martech/AI-product — personalization architecture, attribution modeling, GenAI content pipelines, measurement under privacy constraints
pending_interview.question: You are advising a direct-to-consumer retail brand that runs personalized email campaigns at scale — roughly 8 million subscribers, three sends per week. They currently use a third-party email platform that handles segmentation and send-time optimization. They want to move toward a generative AI content pipeline: dynamically generated subject lines, body copy, and product recommendations tailored to each individual subscriber at the moment of send. Their data team has open-loop click and purchase data, but no identity graph beyond email address. Their head of marketing is concerned about two things: (1) measuring whether the generated content is actually driving incremental revenue, not just clicks, and (2) maintaining compliance with inbox provider deliverability rules as volume and content variation increase. Walk me through how you would design the measurement framework and the content generation architecture to address both concerns — and where you would draw the line between what generative AI handles versus what needs human review.
